title: American AI Security Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American AI Security Act is a federal law that sets out rules and standards for building, testing, and using AI systems so they are safe, reliable, and secure. It is designed to protect national security and public interests by requiring companies and researchers to evaluate and mitigate potential risks before deploying AI technology.

title: Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026 establishes a framework for regulating artificial intelligence within specific industries, ensuring that each sector—such as healthcare, finance, and transportation—has tailored oversight and compliance standards. It aims to balance innovation with public safety by setting sector-specific guidelines, accountability measures, and risk assessment protocols for AI systems.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to prevent AI firms from unfairly raising prices for their services and from manipulating labor markets to suppress wages. The act aims to protect consumers and workers by establishing rules and penalties that curb exploitative pricing and wage-setting practices in the AI industry.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House says Congress should refuse to give extra money or special regulatory help to companies or financial institutions that are on the brink of collapse due to stress in the artificial‑intelligence market. Instead, Congress must focus on providing support to all Americans who have been harmed.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act establishes guidelines for using AI in vocational education and training settings. It aims to protect learners by ensuring that AI tools are safe, fair, and transparent while supporting effective skill development.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 establishes that medical diagnosis, treatment recommendations, and patient care must be performed by licensed human physicians rather than artificial intelligence systems. It imposes strict licensing, accountability, and liability requirements for any AI tools used in healthcare, ensuring patient safety and human oversight.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 is a proposed U.S. law aimed at ensuring AI systems are transparent, safe, and fair. It requires companies to conduct impact assessments and mitigate biases in algorithms that affect people.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This act seeks to protect election integrity by setting rules and safeguards against AI-generated misinformation that could influence voters. It includes measures for monitoring, transparency, and accountability for AI content used in political contexts.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a U.S. federal law aimed at ensuring the development and deployment of AI systems are safe, transparent, and trustworthy. It establishes guidelines, oversight mechanisms, and funding priorities to support research that improves AI reliability while protecting public interests.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 aims to ensure that AI systems used by the Department of Veterans Affairs are open and accountable. It establishes requirements for documenting AI decision processes, publishing transparency reports, and giving veterans clear explanations about how AI affects their services.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is designed to establish clear guidelines and oversight for the use of artificial intelligence in processing Veterans Affairs claims, ensuring transparency and accountability. It aims to protect veterans by mandating rigorous testing, data protection, and recourse mechanisms for decisions impacted by AI systems.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: This act aims to protect consumers from misleading or deceptive use of artificial intelligence, ensuring that AI products and services are clear about their capabilities and limitations. It sets rules and enforcement tools to prevent deceptive practices and safeguard consumer rights in the digital marketplace.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act aims to improve the security and preparedness of AI systems. It includes measures to identify, mitigate, and respond to AI-related risks and vulnerabilities.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act proposes to create a new task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Its goal is to study, develop, and coordinate federal efforts to secure AI systems and protect critical infrastructure from AI‑related cyber threats.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 is a proposed law designed to establish clear guidelines for identifying, assessing, and reducing risks associated with AI systems. It aims to set security standards, enforce compliance, and promote responsible development and use of artificial intelligence.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 aims to regulate and coordinate the development and deployment of physical AI systems. It establishes federal oversight, safety standards, and collaboration mechanisms to ensure that autonomous physical AI technologies operate safely and transparently.
